data.narrative:
QuantWare, a Series B quantum computing company founded by Matt Rijlaarsdam and Alessandro Bruno, operates within a sector comprising 3 public peers (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private competitors including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion. The company has raised $178M to date.

The valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method due to peer-set constraints. Stage-progression methodology, applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yields $338M based on the $178M total raised as a valuation proxy. A peer-median approach proved inapplicable: while 6 quantum computing peers exist in the broader universe, the narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, similar-tier) returned insufficient datapoints (fewer than 3) to support reliable triangulation, making sector-wide median comparison potentially misleading.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $287M to $389M, with a median point of $338M. This range reflects stage-typical progression mechanics rather than market-derived comparables. Key uncertainties include the absence of near-peer financial data sufficient to validate Stage B benchmarks within quantum computing specifically, and the lack of disclosed revenue or unit metrics to ground valuation against operational performance. A future peer-set refresh as the sector matures—particularly if private competitors approach exit or public disclosure—would materially strengthen confidence in this range.
